claim: The Browser Company announced Arc's December 22 sunset and stopped new Arc registrations on October 22, shifting engineering focus to Dia.
verifiedFacts: Arc's official transition page says new accounts stopped October 22 and desktop Arc will stop working December 22, 2026.
The company directs existing users to export or migrate tabs, passwords, profiles and bookmarks to Dia.
The company attributes the decision partly to ongoing browser security maintenance demands.
inference: Creative product interfaces need lifecycle/export contracts and resilient browser QA.
Consultancy implication: browser lifecycle and portability audit for client-facing interactive web experiences.
Project disposition: PRODUCTIZE for MelodicBloom/shader-gallery browser compatibility proof, not a reason to rebuild Arc.
significance: A notable browser discontinuation creates a concrete migration deadline and demonstrates product lifecycle risk.
assumptions: Some client workflows rely on Arc-specific features; none verified for the user's repositories.
knownLimitations: No verified local Arc dependency or migration requirement.
No independent comparative Dia security audit.
